text:
maria_cust_ops: Hey team — Acme (customer-id: acme-prod) opened a high-sev ticket: their API calls are getting 401s and a lot of cross-region latency. They expect eu-west routing but most traffic lands in us-east and hits timeouts.

jamie_support: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste a sample request id and the route key? Also is this only for that API key or all requests for that org?

maria_cust_ops: request_id=rx-20260310-99a8, route_key=acme-prod-gen. Only this org. They started hitting it ~20:20 UTC. Attached minimal curl they ran: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxx" -H "X-Request-ID: rx-20260310-99a8" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=redwood-rl-1
```

lee_eng_infra: Looking at routing logs now. I see a pattern: their sessions have an affinity cookie 'rw_aff' set from us-east with domain=.redwood.ai, but our edge in eu-west is rejecting that cookie due to SameSite mismatch when it's a long-lived session. That causes requests to be treated as stateless and fall through to the default weighted pool.

olga_oncall_sre: Can you paste the failover policy for that route? I want to see priority vs weight and sticky settings. If sticky is enabled but cookie isn't accepted, fallback logic may pick a weight-based target.

jamie_support: I pulled the policy from the console for acme-prod: 
```json
{"sticky": {"enabled": true, "cookie_name": "rw_aff", "ttl_ms": "3600000"}, "targets": [{"region": "eu-west-1", "priority": 1, "weight": "70%"}, {"region": "us-east-1", "priority": 2, "weight": "30%"}]}
```

lee_eng_infra: A few red flags here: 1) ttl_ms is a string not a number (UI bug can send string), 2) weights are percentages as strings with '%' which our older parser doesn't handle (it expects integer weight), and 3) edge cookie handling differs by region due to different CDN versions (eu edge Version B strips SameSite=None in some cases). When weight parsing fails we fall back to equal-priority evaluation which with priority present should be fine, but because of the ttl being a string the sticky path isn't being recorded in the KV store. Net effect — sessions appear sticky-disabled and the runtime picks the first available target from a sorted list that in this case ended up being us-east.

maria_cust_ops: So both cookie domain + parse issues combined? Customer sees auth 401s when routed to us-east because their token is region-bound? They said tokens are minted scoped to eu workloads.

lee_eng_infra: Yes — their tokens contain regional claims enforced by a downstream auth service in eu. If the request hits us-east, auth fails -> 401s. And because traffic traversed cross-region it added 150-400ms latency.

olga_oncall_sre: For a fast mitigation I can flip the route override to force-eu for acme-prod for the next 2 hours and roll back once we confirm the cookie behavior. That will avoid auth 401s and reduce latency. Jamie's ok with notifying the customer?

jamie_support: Please do the override now and I'll message the customer and engineers. Also cc billing_bot — they reported a small billing spike from retries.

deploy_bot: run: apply-route-override --route acme-prod --force-region eu-west-1 --duration 2h --by oncall
deploy_bot: ✅ override applied (run_id: r-20260310-224). Traffic now pinned to eu-west-1.

jamie_support: Notified customer: "We've forced your traffic to eu-west while we investigate; you should see immediate improvements. We will follow up with permanent fix."

lee_eng_infra: For the root fix: plan is three-step — 1) Console fix: stringify -> numeric coercion for ttl_ms in server API, 2) Parser fix: accept percentages and strip '%' to compute integer weight or convert to proportional weight, 3) Edge rollout: harmonize cookie SameSite behavior across CDN versions (or move rw_aff to a domainless token header). I'll open a PR and a canary rollout.

jamie_support: Can you include a repro snippet so we can validate? Customer wants to test locally.

lee_eng_infra: Repro steps: 
1) Create a route with sticky cookie and ttl as string and percent weights (use console or API). 
2) Hit endpoint from eu edge with a client that preserves cookies. Observe rw_aff created by us-east and then request to eu doesn't send cookie. 
3) Curl that forces us-east by altering Host header path — you should see 401. Example: 
```
# set policy via API (bad payload)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/routes -H "Authorization: Bearer infra-test" -d '{"route":"test-az","sticky":{"enabled":true,"cookie_name":"rw_aff","ttl_ms":"3600000"},"targets":[{"region":"eu-west-1","priority":1,"weight":"70%"},{"region":"us-east-1","priority":2,"weight":"30%"}]}'
```

lee_eng_infra: Quick debug query (for oncall): 
```
select t.request_id, t.edge_region, p.targets, p.sticky from routing_logs t join policies p on t.route = p.route where t.request_id = 'rx-20260310-99a8';
```

olga_oncall_sre: I'm on it. I'll also watch for any billing anomalies.

billing_bot: Alert: retry spike detected for org acme-prod between 2026-03-10T20:15:00Z and 2026-03-10T20:40:00Z — estimated extra tokens billed: ~1.2M tokens. Logging ticket to billing with reference rb-9981.

maria_cust_ops: Thanks all. Please keep me posted and I'll relay to Acme. Appreciate the rapid override. :pray:

jamie_support: Postmortem action items noted: console validation for numeric fields, parser robustness for weight formats, cookie SameSite audit, customer comms template. I'll track in the support backlog.

lee_eng_infra: I'll open the infra PR and tag olga for the canary. Expect patch in ~3 hours.

olga_oncall_sre: Override ends at 22:24 UTC (2h). If all good, we'll schedule a safe rollout.

maria_cust_ops: Confirmed Acme sees success after override — latency down and 401s gone. Closing customer ticket pending permanent fix.
